To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the telegraph equation does not describe the CR transport in the presence of magnetic focusing and the “telegraph solution” is not physical.

(i) the “telegraph term” is not inherent in the CR transport problem, but (ii) it may be formally introduced to the solution by converting the fourth order hyperdiffusive term of the Chapman–Enskoff expansion, (iii) the telegraph solution, though formally equivalent to the Chapman–Enscog one, is unphysical and should not be used, (iv) the telegraph term should only be used for a short relaxation phase associated with strong pitch-angle anist
the telegraph and the Chapman–Enskorg approaches are reasonably equivalent, and the telegraph solution, though not physically meaningful during the relaxation period, is not unimportant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation of the CR transport equation.
the CR transport model based upon the telegraph equation, and we have found that it is not consistent with the CR transport problem in the limit of weak scattering.
the derivation of the telegraph equation for the CR transport problem, and the validity of the resulting solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the telegraph approach is a useful approximation only during the relaxation period and that it is not a valid approximation to the CR transport in the long time asymptotic.
the CR transport is diffusive and the “telegraph term” is not an intrinsic feature of CR propagation.
the telegraph equation is not an alternative CR transport equation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the telegraph approach to CR transport, as a whole, is not a viable alternative to the diffusive approximation.
the telegraph equation is a poor model for CR transport.
the “telegraph equation” approach is not a proper asymptotic reduction of CR transport with scattering on magnetic inhomogeneities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the telegraph model is not a physically consistent model for CR propagation.
the telegraph and diffusion models are not equivalent.
the telegraph model, though often useful, is not a fundamental transport equation for CRs.
